questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how AppointmentBooker handles concurrent bookings and cancellations for the same slot? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Three bookings for slot A arrive at once. The first one's repository save rejects. What happens to the other two?
choices: They hang forever because the lock is never released
They run in order after the first finishes, because release() is called in finally
They run in parallel because the failed call clears the lock map
They fail with the same error as the first

questions.prompt: Bookings for slot A and slot B arrive at the same time. How do they interact?
choices: They are serialized behind one global lock
Slot B waits until slot A's tail entry is deleted
They can run concurrently because locks are keyed by slotId
Slot B is rejected while slot A is locked

questions.prompt: Why does runExclusive check this.tails.get(key) === tail before deleting?
choices: To avoid removing a newer waiter's tail, which would let a later caller skip the queue
To prevent a memory leak when fn throws
Because Map.delete throws if the key is missing
To make the first caller always run before the others
